    01 / Choose your learning

    Places to find physician CME

    Start with the requirement you need to meet. Before enrolling, check the activity’s credit statement, eligibility, total cost and deadline to claim credit.

    Online activity directory

    CME Passport

    Search activities by accredited providers. Check credit type, registration eligibility and the provider’s current activity page.

    Free search; activity fees vary.

    Explore CME Passport ↗

    Sources: CME Passport activity search · ACCME: how CME Passport works · ACCME: CME for maintenance of certification

    Online courses and recorded learning

    CDC TRAIN

    Find public-health learning with physician CME available on selected courses. TCEO retired at the end of 2025; start with CDC TRAIN.

    Free CE on many courses; check each listing.

    Explore CDC TRAIN ↗

    Sources: CDC TRAIN: current learning platform · CDC continuing-education credit types

    Online training and educational events

    PCSS-MOUD

    Explore SAMHSA-supported substance-use training. For MATE, check the specific course’s eligibility, hours and completion evidence.

    Free training.

    Explore PCSS-MOUD ↗

    Sources: SAMHSA PCSS-MOUD training · SAMHSA MATE training resources

    Courses, articles, videos and audio

    AMA Ed Hub

    Browse physician education and inspect the CME label. Free reading does not always include the quiz or credit claim.

    Free account; some credit requires membership, subscription or a fee.

    Explore AMA Ed Hub ↗

    Sources: AMA Ed Hub: access, costs and claiming credit

    Live and on-demand activities

    AOA CME resources

    Find live and on-demand osteopathic education. Verify the listed AOA category and your board’s acceptance.

    Check activity pricing and membership access.

    Explore AOA CME resources ↗

    Sources: AOA CME resources and search

    These are independent resources. Availability and prices can change; CredentialDOMD does not award CME credit or guarantee acceptance of an activity.

    03 / Understand what counts

    CME, without the guesswork

    State licensure, specialty certification and DEA registration can ask for different things. Keep each requirement visible.

    Start with the requirementCheck the credit typePlan for each licenseUnderstand DEA MATESeparate CME from board certificationUse CME PassportKeep usable evidenceBuild a renewal plan

    Start with the requirement

    Choose learning that fits the obligation you need to meet.

    CME supports continued professional learning. License renewal, specialty certification and employer credentialing can ask for different evidence.

    1. Identify the organization receiving your credit.
    2. Check its cycle, accepted categories and required topics.
    3. Check the activity’s credit statement before enrolling.

    Sources: AMA: checking activity credit statements

    Check the credit type

    Read the certificate’s exact designation.

    AMA PRA Category 1 Credit and AOA categories use different systems. An accredited provider can also publish material that does not award CME.

    AOA categories include 1-A, 1-B, 2-A and 2-B. Keep the category actually awarded; confirm the category mix your receiving board requires.

    1. Check the provider in the ACCME directory when applicable.
    2. Read the activity’s designation and maximum credit.
    3. Keep AMA, AOA, MOC and participation labels distinct.

    Sources: ACCME: find an accredited provider · AMA PRA credit requirements · AOA CME policies: 2025–2027 cycle

    Plan for each license

    Check each license separately.

    Use the correct medical or osteopathic board.

    1. Record each license’s cycle.
    2. Confirm accepted categories, topics and exceptions.
    3. Review each activity against each intended use.

    Sources: FSMB: find your licensing board

    Understand DEA MATE

    Keep the one-time federal training requirement separate from recurring CME.

    At the first applicable DEA registration or renewal on or after June 27, 2023, covered practitioners attest to meeting an accepted training standard. Solely veterinary practitioners are excluded.

    Routes include specified addiction certification, qualifying recent education, or at least eight hours of eligible training. Earlier eligible training and cumulative sessions may count.

    Eligible DEA training may also count toward state requirements when the state accepts it. Check each requirement before taking duplicate training.

    1. Read the DEA eligibility guidance for your situation.
    2. Check the training source and keep completion evidence.
    3. Do not automatically repeat eight hours at every renewal.

    Sources: DEA MATE training questions and answers · SAMHSA MATE training resources · U.S. Code: DEA registration and training, section 823(m)

    Separate CME from board certification

    Credit hours alone do not describe an entire certification program.

    ABMS member boards set specialty-specific continuing-certification programs. Some CME activities also offer designated MOC credit. AOA certification uses its own OCC requirements.

    1. Check your certifying board’s current program and whether your licensing board recognizes certification activities toward CME.
    2. Confirm the activity’s board-specific recognition and reporting requirements.
    3. Keep board points separate from CME hours unless the activity explicitly awards both.

    Sources: ABMS continuing-certification standards · ACCME: CME for maintenance of certification · AOA CME policies: 2025–2027 cycle

    Use CME Passport

    Understand what appears in your record and how to bring it here.

    Providers report completion to ACCME with your permission and matching information. Physicians cannot self-report completion into CME Passport.

    1. Ask the provider whether it reports your credit.
    2. Check your Passport record after reporting.
    3. Download your transcript and use Import transcript in CredentialDOMD. Review every row before saving.

    Sources: ACCME: how CME Passport works · CredentialDOMD product walkthroughs

    Keep usable evidence

    Keep credit easy to verify.

    Keep the original certificate or transcript. A saved file or progress bar is not a board decision.

    1. Review the provider, completion date, credit and category.
    2. Check imported fields and duplicates.
    3. Keep readable backups.

    Sources: CredentialDOMD product walkthroughs · AMA: checking activity credit statements

    Build a renewal plan

    Work backward from your deadline.

    Leave time to claim credit and resolve missing evidence.

    1. Confirm your board’s cycle and deadline.
    2. Review your evidence and remaining activities.
    3. Check claim deadlines.
    4. Complete the renewal application.

    Sources: FSMB: find your licensing board · AMA Ed Hub: access, costs and claiming credit

    04 / Answers to common questions

    The details that trip people up

    How many CME hours do I need?

    Check your licensing and certifying boards. This center does not assign a universal hour total or determine individual compliance.

    Sources: FSMB: find your licensing board · ABMS continuing-certification standards

    Can I find CME without paying?

    Start with CDC TRAIN and PCSS-MOUD. Check that the specific activity awards physician CME and includes the certificate or credit claim at no charge.

    Sources: CDC TRAIN: current learning platform · CDC continuing-education credit types · SAMHSA PCSS-MOUD training

    How do I know an activity awards physician CME?

    Look for its credit designation, maximum available credit and completion requirements. Provider accreditation alone does not make every resource a CME activity.

    Sources: AMA: checking activity credit statements · ACCME: find an accredited provider

    Are AMA and AOA categories interchangeable?

    Do not automatically convert AMA Category 1 into AOA Category 1-A. Preserve the original credit type and confirm acceptance with the receiving organization.

    Sources: AOA CME policies: 2025–2027 cycle · AOA CME questions and reporting

    What is AMA PRA Category 2 Credit?

    Physicians may self-document qualifying learning that is not certified for Category 1 under AMA criteria. It must be relevant to practice, non-promotional and meet the AMA’s educational and ethical standards. Check whether the receiving board accepts it; reading alone does not create Category 1 credit.

    Sources: AMA: understanding Category 2 credit

    Are MOC points the same as CME hours?

    They are distinct credit designations. An activity may award both; verify each amount and board recognition rather than converting points into CME hours.

    Sources: ACCME: CME for maintenance of certification

    Can one activity help with more than one license?

    Confirm dates, topics and acceptance for each license. Do not assume reciprocity.

    Sources: FSMB: find your licensing board

    Can extra credits roll into my next cycle?

    Check the receiving board’s carryover rule before relying on surplus credit. Do not assume rollover.

    Sources: FSMB: find your licensing board

    Can I claim an exemption or waiver?

    Ask the relevant board about eligibility, evidence and approval. An AOA certification waiver does not change state-license requirements.

    Sources: AOA CME policies: 2025–2027 cycle

    What if my certificate is missing?

    Check your provider account or request a replacement from the activity organizer. Keep the completion details while you resolve it. Do not invent a certificate.

    Sources: AMA: checking activity credit statements

    Can I claim credit after a course expires?

    Check the activity’s credit-claim deadline and contact its provider. Reading material while it was available does not establish that a later claim is accepted.

    Sources: AMA Ed Hub: access, costs and claiming credit

    How long should I keep CME records?

    Use your board’s retention and audit instructions. This center does not prescribe a universal retention period. Keep readable backups.

    Sources: FSMB: find your licensing board

    Why is an activity missing from CME Passport?

    Its provider may not have reported it, or matching details may need correction. Contact the provider; you cannot add completion credit yourself in Passport.

    Sources: ACCME: how CME Passport works

    Does CredentialDOMD automatically sync with Passport?

    The available workflow is to download your Passport transcript and import it. Review the proposed entries before saving; this is not automatic account synchronization.

    Sources: CredentialDOMD product walkthroughs

    Do I repeat MATE training every DEA renewal?

    MATE is a one-time attestation requirement. Check the DEA guidance if your training history or eligibility is uncertain. State requirements remain separate.

    Sources: DEA MATE training questions and answers

    Can earlier training satisfy MATE?

    Earlier eligible training, including qualifying DATA-waiver training, may count. Confirm the content and training source under DEA guidance and keep the evidence.

    Sources: DEA MATE training questions and answers

    Do CredentialDOMD tutorials award CME?

    No. Our walkthroughs teach app tasks and use demo data. They do not award CME, MOC points or DEA training credit.

    Sources: CredentialDOMD product walkthroughs

    Does the app confirm that I am compliant?

    Its calculation depends on your saved records and rules on file. Review dates, categories and applicability, and confirm unresolved questions with the receiving board.

    Sources: CredentialDOMD product walkthroughs

    Does reported CME renew my license automatically?

    Reported credit is not proof that renewal is complete. Check your board’s application and confirmation requirements.

    Sources: FSMB: find your licensing board
